subject: Business
title: Shell Money and Commodity Currencies
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Shell Money and Commodity Currencies.

hook.text: Cowrie shells were money in China, India, and Africa for over 3,000 years. Longer than any modern currency.

buildup.text: Commodity money uses objects with inherent value or scarcity: shells, salt, tea bricks, even cattle.

discovery.text: Good commodity money is durable, portable, divisible, and scarce. Shells checked most of these boxes.

twist.text: When Europeans brought boatloads of cowrie shells to Africa, they inflated the supply. The currency collapsed.

climax.text: The lesson: any money's value depends on controlled supply. Flood the market and trust evaporates.

punchline.text: Money works only as long as everyone agrees it's scarce.

quiz.question: Why did cowrie shell currency collapse in parts of Africa?
options: Europeans imported massive quantities, flooding the supply
Shells became too fragile to use

details.summary: Cowrie shells served as currency across Africa, South Asia, and the Pacific for thousands of years, valued for their durability, portability, and difficulty to counterfeit. Other commodity currencies included beads, cattle, and textiles, each reflecting local value systems.
details.whyItMatters: Commodity currencies demonstrate the universal human need for a medium of exchange and reveal the properties any successful money must have: acceptance, divisibility, durability, and limited supply in the local context.
takeaways: Cowrie shells functioned as money across three continents for millennia
Commodity money must be durable, portable, divisible, and accepted by all
Different cultures chose whatever scarce item best met local monetary needs

faq.question: Why were cowrie shells so widely used as money?
faq.answer: They were small, durable, easy to count, uniform in size, difficult to forge, and could not be easily found in most trading regions. Their scarcity away from tropical oceans gave them value in continental Africa and interior Asia where they had to be imported.

faq.question: What caused cowrie shell money to eventually collapse?
faq.answer: European colonial traders imported massive quantities of cowrie shells from the Maldives, flooding local markets and causing hyperinflation in African economies. The oversupply destroyed their scarcity value, just as printing too much fiat money causes inflation today.
